A repo-wide grep of `isPersistenceEnabled` over all .ts/.tsx/.js/.mjs/.mts files yields only wafflebase-doc-store.ts (definition/use), wafflebase-doc-store-cleanup.test.ts:807/838/852 — which builds its own stores with its own `() => enabled` option, i.e. store-level behavior not the wiring — and the provider. Greps of get/setOfflinePersistenceEnabled across all test files surface only the preference module, offline-erase, use-durable-document (election), and the sync-status chip; none exercises a store the provider constructed, and there are no e2e/spec tests for it. Deleting the option from the provider would leave every test green while the still-mounted durable client re-writes the open document onto the disk the user just asked to clear — a silently weakened data/privacy guard, so major under the test-adequacy rubric.
